niche.habitat: Deep hydrothermal vent chimneys and anoxic brine pools
niche.diet: Chemotrophic bacteria and small vent-fauna; extracts energy from thermal gradients

body: Armored carapace with bifurcated gill-plates housing induction coils; ampullary electroreceptive pores along the snout; magnetite-reinforced joints

chains.trait: Gill-membrane induction coils transmit short-range pulses
links: Coils modulate B-field to induce currents in neighbors
Conductive ocean (F9) diffuses magnetic fields in microseconds; range limited to 2 cm 'in-shield' contact
Why beats sound: Hydrothermal roar and ambient flow noise mask acoustic calls; magnetic induction provides a low-noise, directional private channel immune to water turbulence
Why beats light: Abyssal darkness; bioluminescence (F15) attracts predators and wastes energy; magnetic pulses are stealthy and energetically efficient at contact
Energy cost: 0.8 W pulse; harvested from thermal gradient via thermoelectric symbionts

skill.effect: The creature strikes and delivers a sharp electric jolt that ripples outward as a disorienting magnetic pulse. Nearby foes may stagger and falter in their movements for a short while.

chains.weakness: Conductivity dependence: In low-conductivity brine pools or dry zones, range drops to 0 and induction fails.
observe: Gill-plates pulse with rhythmic water displacement
Target creature exhibits a sudden spasm when coils touch
Water around coils shimmers due to local induction heating

journal.en: A secret passed through the water's skin, felt as a ghost-spasm.

plausibility.summary: Hard-cap Inductive Tap and social pulses to skin-to-skin contact in conductive brine; treat thermoelectric symbionts as highly speculative; note induction heating observables only at very high local |dB/dt|.
fixes: Hard-cap Inductive Tap and social pulses to skin-to-skin contact in conductive brine; treat thermoelectric symbionts as highly speculative; note induction heating observables only at very high local |dB/dt|.

analogues.organism: Weakly electric fish electrocommunication and jamming responses (E-field, not B-field)—Bullock 1982; hagfish ampullary electroreception—Hagiwara 1973
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded
see the cited works; chain wording is the council's own

links: Complements magnetic sense to locate prey and predators
Conductive water (F9) transmits bioelectric signals efficiently
Essential for hunting in total darkness where magnetic comms require contact

skill.effect: The creature's sensory pores hum as it traces the faint bioelectric fields of nearby life, causing hidden foes to shimmer with visible outlines. This natural awareness makes it easier to track and engage creatures that try to conceal themselves.

chains.weakness: Noise: High electromagnetic interference from nearby vent activity or magnetic storms masks bioelectric signals.
observe: Snout pores twitch rhythmically, sampling the water
Creature tracks invisible prey with precise head movements
Prey appears to glow faintly to the Ostracilo

journal.en: It smells the heartbeat of the world.

plausibility.summary: High-conductivity hydrothermal matrix (F9, F10) supports passive detection of prey muscle and epithelial dipoles at multi-meter range, matching ampullary electroreception in elasmobranchs and the world’s F14 ampullary/electrolocation stack. Vent EM noise can mask weak bioelectric cues during magnetic storms—reasonable weakness.
fixes: High-conductivity hydrothermal matrix (F9, F10) supports passive detection of prey muscle and epithelial dipoles at multi-meter range, matching ampullary electroreception in elasmobranchs and the world’s F14 ampullary/electrolocation stack. Vent EM noise can mask weak bioelectric cues during magnetic storms—reasonable weakness.

analogues.organism: Shark ampullae of Lorenzini—prey bioelectric fields at meters; ray/skate passive electroreception—Bullock 1982
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

links: Provides torsional strength against 1.49 g gravity (F3) and hydrostatic pressure (F9)
Magnetite also reduces net magnetic signature via helical alignment (F16)
Dual benefit: armor and magnetic stealth for ambush

skill.effect: The creature anchors itself firmly and hardens its shell, causing its magnetic signature to fade from view and dampening external field disruptions. While it remains perfectly still to maintain this cover, it becomes temporarily unable to strike.

chains.weakness: Mass: Heavier than analogues, reducing dodge chance against fast predators.
observe: Shell plates reflect light with a dull, non-metallic sheen
Creature moves silently despite heavy armor
Magnetic anomalies deflect around its body

plausibility.summary: Keep armor benefit primary; downgrade Magnetic Stealth to reduced detectability (weaker net moment), not anomaly deflection; accept mass/dodge penalty as stated.
fixes: Keep armor benefit primary; downgrade Magnetic Stealth to reduced detectability (weaker net moment), not anomaly deflection; accept mass/dodge penalty as stated.

analogues.organism: Magnetotactic bacteria single-domain chains—Frankel, Blakemore; chiton and limpet magnetite in radular teeth—from memory, unverified
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded
see the cited works; chain wording is the council's own

links: Uses magnetic field gradients to navigate vent networks
Follows stable anomaly corridors (F18) to find food and thermal plumes
Avoids field spikes (F5) that could disrupt neural function
Cooperative breeding groups maintain formation via magnetic pulses

skill.effect: The creature flows effortlessly through magnetic barriers and field-dependent obstacles as if they were mere mist. Its steady migration naturally quickens the pace of nearby allies who follow in its wake.

chains.weakness: Field spikes: Sudden storm spikes (F5) can scatter the migration path, causing disorientation.
observe: Creature aligns perfectly with invisible field lines
Group moves in unison, coordinated by subtle gill pulses
Pathing avoids areas of high magnetic noise

journal.en: It walks the invisible rivers of the crust.

plausibility.summary: Corridor Glide navigation: plausible; ally speed buff from gill pulses only within 2 cm contact chain, not 3 m through seawater.
fixes: Corridor Glide navigation: plausible; ally speed buff from gill pulses only within 2 cm contact chain, not 3 m through seawater.

analogues.organism: Sea turtles and fish open-ocean magnetoreception along field intensity gradients; magnetotactic bacteria along field lines—Blakemore 1975
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

relations.note: Ostracilo evolved analogous coil-structures in a conductive medium; Cobrezo coils are air-optimized, Ostracilo coils are induction-optimized.
Both use magnetic comms but in different media; Cobrezo uses air for directional pulses, Ostracilo uses induction for contact stealth.

body_plan.origin: Vent-mat grazer diverging into a predatory niche

temperament: Patient, territorial, subtly social with kin
secrets: Prey-stun: Inductive pulses can trigger the electroreceptors of small prey, causing a momentary paralysis at contact range.
Symbiont-harvest: Ostracilo can absorb the magnetic memory of a dead rival by consuming its coils, gaining a temporary bonus to identify magnetic traps.
moments: In the vent's roar, a partner drifts blind, its sensors fouled by thermal shear. A single magnetic tap from the Ostracilo guides it home, a ghost-spasm in the gills that says, 'Follow,' cutting through the chaos without a sound.

journal.en: The water hums, but only the coils answer.
In the dark, the field is the only truth.
